items.event_time_ist: late Tuesday night, Oct 13 local Saudi time (early hours of Oct 14 IST)
items.summary: A Houthi ballistic missile hit Saudi Aramco's executive headquarters office complex in Dhahran late Tuesday; a company source told Reuters an office tower's top three floors were damaged and caught fire (blaze later put out), while the Saudi energy ministry confirmed only a limited fire and no injuries. The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted the missile over Dhahran, with fragments falling on a residential area, and also destroyed three cruise missiles and two drones aimed at Riyadh and the south — debris wounded four people in Riyadh and damaged 15 homes. Hours earlier the coalition struck the Houthi-run Yemen Petroleum Company's Sabah fuel depot in Sanaa (Houthis: two civilians killed, two injured) after urging evacuations; Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree had threatened a 'harsh and painful' response naming the Aramco HQ as a target. Brent climbed toward $106 on the Saudi supply risk (+0.8% to $106.58 by 0030 GMT Oct 14, WTI $94.94).
items.title: Houthi missile hits Aramco's Dhahran HQ complex; Saudi strikes Sanaa fuel depot in retaliatory exchange

items.event_time_ist: strategy adopted ~10 days ago (early Oct 2026); disclosed Oct 14
items.summary: Two senior Iranian officials told Reuters that about ten days ago Tehran adopted new tactics — a change in the type and pace of attacks on ships it deems in violation of its Hormuz restrictions — with an explicit aim to keep global oil prices high and influence the Nov 3 US midterm elections: 'The aim is to frustrate efforts by the United States and its allies to bring down global oil prices.' The officials said the decision was taken at the highest levels, that Iran will expand operations beyond Hormuz into the Gulf of Oman and farther afield, and warned 'it will be complete closure soon.' A US military official corroborated one tactic shift: after the US destroyed much of Iran's radar, the IRGC began using unarmed spotters in small boats and dhows to identify targets including US naval vessels; last week US forces confronted one such dhow, ordered its crew off, and destroyed it (no casualties). Maritime security sources count at least five Hormuz-area incidents in the past 48 hours, and the US Navy-led JMIC kept its threat level at 'severe.'
items.title: Iran shifted Hormuz attack tactics ~10 days ago to keep oil high and sway US midterms, officials tell Reuters

items.summary: The US blockade has kept Iranian seaborne crude exports at zero through all of October, per energy-intelligence firm Vortexa — exports fell to zero in the second week of September from ~230,000 bpd and stayed there; 43 million barrels of Iranian crude sit trapped west of the Strait of Hormuz, with 83 million barrels total on the water. Iran's LPG exports fell 48% month-on-month, lowest since at least January 2023. Vortexa's Claire Jungman: the blockade 'is doing what years of sanctions never managed.' Russia now makes up 80% of 'high-risk exports' (Iran, Russia, Venezuela), whose combined 4.73M bpd in September was down from 6.39M a year earlier.
